about: Film v5, the use-case cut (approved by the owner, 5 Oct): one narrator pitches one concrete use case and never says the wake word; customer and add-on lines are Amazon Polly (video/voice/polly-v5.json), word for word from the Household Orders runs. Numbers from the same runs and from PR #27's CI.

lines.text: You've built a grocery add-on for Amazon's voice assistant. A customer says:
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, opening a short story about a developer. Clear and friendly, unhurried, a small lift on 'A customer says' to hand over to the customer's voice. Never salesy, never cheesy.

lines.text: Say the assistant hears fifty. Your add-on answers:
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, a quiet 'what if' that builds a little tension, handing over to the add-on's voice. Clear, unhurried. Never salesy.

lines.text: Fifty dollars of fruit, and nobody noticed. When you tested it by typing, this never came up.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, a dry, knowing beat on 'and nobody noticed', then matter-of-fact. Clear, unhurried. Never salesy.

lines.text: This is Hearsay. An add-on is an MCP server: the part you write. Hearsay plays what customers say against it, as said and misheard, checks every reply, and fails the build before it goes wrong out loud.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, introducing the product with quiet pride, a short pause after 'This is Hearsay'. Clear and precise, every term easy to follow. Never salesy, never cheesy.

lines.text: The assistant listens, picks a tool, calls your server, and speaks the reply.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, walking through four steps with a light beat between them. Clear and calm.

lines.text: Hearsay plays the assistant's part from your test: the words, the mishearings, and the tool call you expect. Then it checks what your server says back.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, explaining the clever part simply. Clear and precise, a light beat between the three things it plays.

lines.text: No microphone, no API keys, the same result every time.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, three short benefits with a beat between them. Calm, assured. Never salesy.

lines.text: Replies are graded by the rules Amazon published for add-ons: half a second per tool call, short replies, no code read aloud, five options at most, and no payment without naming what and how much.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, running through a short checklist, a light beat between the items. Clear and precise.

lines.text: Here's a real run against our demo grocery add-on, built with these flaws on purpose. The customer allowed fifty dollars of groceries today.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, starting a live demo, honest and plain about the demo add-on. Clear, unhurried.

lines.text: Fifty dollars of fruit, added without a word. A no that placed the order anyway. Twenty problems: the build fails.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, calling out what the run found, a beat between the findings, firm on 'the build fails'. Never shouty.

lines.text: The fixed add-on, same tests. It checks every amount against that budget, and says why it won't:
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, showing the after shot, handing over to the add-on's voice at the end. Clear, pleased.

lines.text: Zero errors.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, a short, satisfied payoff. Calm.

lines.text: Hearsay runs on every code change. On GitHub, this change let fifty dollars of fruit slip past the budget.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, explaining a real example. Clear and precise.

lines.text: Hearsay failed the check.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, a matter-of-fact beat. Calm.

lines.text: One fix, and it passes.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, a light, happy payoff. Calm.

lines.text: Hearsay is an MCP server itself, with two Agent Skills. Your coding agent uses them to draft tests for you to review, run them, fix your code, and run them again until they pass, without changing your tests.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, presenting a second way to use the product as a real feature, not a bonus. Clear and precise.

lines.text: And it can't cheat: your tests are locked.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, a confident aside. Calm, assured.

lines.text: Change one, and the run fails.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, finishing the thought plainly. Calm.

lines.text: Hearsay is open source. No keys, no account. Clone it, and your first run takes a minute.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, practical and inviting. Clear, unhurried. Never salesy.

lines.text: Hearsay. Hear it before your customers do.
lines.direction: Warm, confident presenter of a product keynote, the closing tagline, warm and assured, a small pause after 'Hearsay'. Never cheesy.
